inline_comments.comment: The documented default value is wrong. This line says `Default: \`true\`` but the actual implementation in `common-preset.ts` sets `changeDetection: false`, and the JSDoc `@default false` in `core-common.ts` agrees. This directly contradicts the code and will mislead users who rely on the docs to understand the feature's out-of-the-box behaviour. Change to `Default: \`false\``.

The `TODO: Turn to true before 10.4 release` note is embedded in user-facing JSDoc that will appear in IDE hover tooltips for every Storybook consumer who inspects this type. Release scheduling notes like this belong in a GitHub issue, the PR description, or an internal tracking ticket — not in a shipped type definition. Remove the TODO from the JSDoc or replace it with a link to a tracking issue, and record the timeline elsewhere.

The JSDoc description 'Enable change detection' is too minimal to be useful. Per project convention, every boolean flag in `features` must include a brief description explaining what the feature does and its behavioural impact. Based on the codebase, this flag appears to relate to Angular OnPush change detection support. A more useful description would be something like: 'Enable automatic change detection for Angular components using `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`. When enabled, Storybook calls `ChangeDetectorRef.markForCheck()` to ensure args updates are reflected.' Users who do not already know what this flag does will get no actionable information from the current description.

general_comments.comment: No automated tests are included: all test checkboxes in the PR checklist are unchecked and no test files appear in the diff. Even though this is a feature-flag stub, a minimal unit test asserting that the `features` preset includes `changeDetection: false` by default (matching the pattern of other feature-flag tests in the project) would prevent a future accidental default-flip from going undetected and would have caught the docs/code default mismatch described in the inline comment above.

The PR description does not include manual testing steps, which the checklist marks as mandatory for all contributions. Even for a flag that is currently a no-op (default `false` with no consuming logic found), the testing section should at minimum state explicitly: 'No manual testing is needed because enabling the flag has no user-visible effect yet; the implementation will be added in a follow-up PR.' This keeps the contribution process consistent and avoids ambiguity for reviewers.
